conventions: Clefted questions (JOB.39.26, JOB.39.27). Where the ASV clefts a question, the interrogative particle takes the single fronted 'Is' as both question auxiliary and copula (rules 17, 20); the dummy 'it' is its own added unit, headed on itself, because rule 20's cleft sentence heads the dummy on a copula that here belongs to the particle; and the cleft relative 'that' is added under rule 55. Read the clause the relative opens before placing it: a kiy or other subordinator standing at the head of a further coordinated clause is not what it answers to, and where the ASV writes no word at that clause's own head the subordinator is unrepresented. The corpus aligns an interrogative particle to 'is it' as one unit at EZK.20.3 and HAB.2.13; that competing reading was named and rule 20's added-dummy sentence followed.

A supplied 'when' before an infinitive construct the ASV recasts as a finite clause stays inside that infinitive's unit and is never added, whichever morpheme licenses it. Where the infinitive is the nomen rectum of 'et, the construct relation licenses it (rules 19, 52) - JOB.39.1 s004, JOB.39.2 s007. Where no 'et and no preposition stands, the word is part of the infinitive's own recasting, as rule 46 keeps a supplied relative with a recast nominal - JOB.39.1 s007, 'canst thou mark when the hinds do calve'. Rule 55's added subordinator governs a clause the Hebrew writes, and an infinitive construct is not one.

Rule 31's tie-reading for this chapter's animal names: the ASV's class noun carries the lexeme and the modifier beside it is the ASV's specifier, so 'the wild ox' heads on ox (39.9, 39.10), 'the wild ass' and 'the swift ass' on ass (39.5), 'the wild goats' on goats (39.1) and 'the quivering mane' on mane (39.19). Where the English noun is instead a generic the ASV supplied to complete the phrase, the same subtraction moves the head the other way: 'young ones', 'the open field', 'the salt land', 'dwelling place', 'the armed men' and 'threshing floor' all head on the modifier.

A preposition the ASV supplies before a second bare noun is placed by rule 33's closing test, and the chapter falls on both sides of it. Where the English predicate admits no other word, the preposition is the verb's under rule 44: 'hast thou clothed his neck with the quivering mane' (39.19) and 'hath deprived her of wisdom' (39.17). Where the word states what the noun contributes and another would have served, it is the noun's under rule 33: 'with his band' (39.10) and 'On the cliff' (39.28), where sela' carries no preposition in the Hebrew at all.

Supplied possessives are split by what they stand on. On a noun the Hebrew writes, a supplied possessive is added under rule 18's closing sentence: 'his might' (39.19, italic) and 'his strength' (39.21). Inside a light verb's supplied complement that English cannot write without one, it belongs to the verb's rendering as rule 30 keeps the pronouns of a particle's idiomatic formula: 'maketh her home' for yitlonan (39.28), headed on home under rule 44. The competing reading - 'her' added under rule 18's closing sentence - is named in that unit.

The chapter's three renderings of shuv are divided by rule 44's subtraction rather than by the shape of the English verb phrase, and one of them departs from that rule's own example. 'They go forth and return not again' (39.4) leaves 'again' added, because 'return' has already written the returning; 'neither turneth he back' (39.22) and 'he will bring home thy seed' (39.12) keep their particles, because 'turneth' and 'bring' alone do not.
report: One genuine split, in the clefted-question couplet JOB.39.26-27. Both verses are the same ASV construction: the interrogative particle takes the single fronted 'Is' (rules 17, 20), a dummy 'it' stands beside it, and a relative 'that' opens the clause carrying the predication. JOB.39.26 marks that 'that' added as the cleft relative; JOB.39.27 hands the identical word to the kiy of s008, which stands not in the clefted clause yagbiah nasher but at the head of the further coordinated clause yariym qinno, for which the ASV writes only 'And maketh'. That is a reach across a clause boundary of the kind rule 16 forbids for a marker and rule 42 for a surplus 'and', and rule 20's cleft carve-out reaches a subordinator standing in the clefted clause, not one a clause on. Patched JOB.39.27: t006 'that' becomes added, s008 becomes unrepresented. JOB.39.26 is unchanged and is the model.

Checked and cleared as source-licensed rather than splits: the eight interrogative-particle treatments (JOB.39.1's particle is unrepresented because the ASV marks that question by inversion alone, which is rule 17's own case; every other verse writes a fronted auxiliary, and where the second-question particle already holds a written connective - 'Or' in 39.9 and 39.10, 'But' in 39.13 - the auxiliary correctly stays with the verb); the le and be buckets, each read off whether the ASV spent a word on that preposition's own relation (rule 40) rather than off the lemma; the article buckets, each read off which word the ASV's 'the' stands before; the three shuv renderings, divided consistently by rule 44's subtraction ('again' surplus after 'return' in 39.4, 'back' and 'home' completing the lexeme in 39.22 and 39.12); and the two supplied resumptive subject pronouns folded into written nouns under rule 25 (39.13, 39.16) against the 'she' of 39.16 left added, which is right because s001 already holds the pronoun written for its own person and number.

Read the dump end to end for the blind spot the lemma table cannot see, the added units. The chapter's supplied 'that', 'it', 'Or', 'And', 'Though', 'his', 'them', 'it', 'soundeth' and 'the grain of' all count out consistently against the morphemes standing in their clauses; the one exception was the JOB.39.27 'that' now patched. The two supplied prepositions before a second bare noun fall on opposite sides of rule 33's closing test on purpose - 'clothed his neck with' (39.19) and 'deprived her of' (39.17) are English valency and go to the verb, 'with his band' (39.10) and 'On the cliff' (39.28) state what the noun contributes and go to the noun - and that judgment is now in the log rather than left to be rediscovered.

BSB disagreements: none is an error. All eight are the documented convention difference on function morphemes the ASV's recasting leaves nothing to say - the four bare-object le/be prepositions of 39.7, 39.11, 39.18 and 39.29, the be of 39.17 whose object the ASV promotes to a bare direct object, and the datives of 39.18 and 39.19 written as bare English indirect objects, every one of them rule 40's condition rather than a lemma reading. The JOB.39.1 interrogative particle is rule 17's inversion-only sentence verbatim ('Knowest thou the time', no auxiliary written). No accepted edge was changed to move the 97.4% figure.

No promotions. The interrogative cleft did expose a gap - rule 20's cleft sentence says the dummy and its copula are one added unit headed on the copula, which cannot be followed where the copula has gone to the interrogative particle and the dummy stands alone - but the corpus contradicts the amendment that gap invites: it already aligns the interrogative particle to 'is it' as one unit headed on 'is' at EZK.20.3 and HAB.2.13. Rule 20's own sentence marking a cleft 'it' added is what this chapter followed in both verses, so the chapter is consistent with the binding text and a rule the corpus contradicts is worse than none. Recorded as a convention instead.
